status: implemented-and-isolated-verified; no real manager was updated

implementation.channelModel: UpdateChannel distinguishes Standalone, Corepack and PythonPackage, derived from evidence next to the resolved command rather than from the static catalog
implementation.corepack: A npm/pnpm/yarn command file whose body names corepack is treated as a Corepack shim; self-update is refused because Corepack pins the active version
implementation.pythonPackage: A uv binary that sits beside pip.exe with an interpreter one level up is treated as pip-installed; uv self update is refused because it would overwrite files pip owns
implementation.evidenceRule: An unreadable shim is not evidence of anything: the checker falls back to Standalone rather than guessing, so a locked or missing file never fabricates a blocker
implementation.wiring: The check runs at the top of self_update_command, so both the preview and the executor refuse with the same reason and the preview can never promise a blocked update

defectsFixed: The first version of the pip-installed uv check looked for python.exe beside uv.exe, but pip installs it into <Python>/Scripts with the interpreter one level up. The fixture caught the miss and the check now looks in both places.

fixtures.name: pkgtools::tests::corepack_and_pip_installed_managers_refuse_self_update_with_a_specific_reason
asserts: a pnpm.cmd whose body names corepack reports UpdateChannel::Corepack and is refused with a Corepack-specific reason
a real pnpm bundle at a standalone path reports Standalone and still yields `self-update`
a missing shim is not treated as Corepack evidence (falls back to Standalone)
a uv.exe beside pip.exe with the interpreter one level up reports PythonPackage and is refused with the `pip install --upgrade uv` suggestion

notVerified: No real Corepack-managed or pip-installed manager exists in this environment, so both branches were exercised only through fixtures
The Corepack shim heuristic reads the launcher body; a shim that invokes corepack indirectly (through another wrapper) would not be detected
npm and yarn already validate their own prefix before this change; only the channel check was added on top
limitations: composer and bun have no installation-shape check yet: both are still treated as Standalone
The check inspects files only; it never runs `corepack which` or queries the interpreter, so it cannot see a shim replaced after resolution
A refusal is reported through the existing blocked path, so the UI text is a plain reason rather than a dedicated installation-shape badge
